Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:10:1.english: For an animal - [For] a communal offering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:1:1.hebrew: כיון שזכה כו' - אם נתנו בתורת חליפין, נקנו חליפין ללוקח במשיכה שמשך בעל המקח את זה. ואשמועינן דתורת חליפין במטלטלין, ולמימר דאע"ג דליתנהו כלי אלא מטלטלין בעלמא — הוו חליפין, ולא מטבע אתא לאשמועינן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:1:1.english: Once this [party] acquired, etc. - If he gave it in the manner of an exchange, the exchanged item is acquired by the buyer through the pulling that the owner of the merchandise performed on this [item]. And [the Mishnah] teaches us that the law of exchange applies to movable property, meaning to say that even though they are not a vessel, but merely ordinary movable property, they effect an exchange; and it did not come to teach us [about] a coin.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:1:2.english: [The wording] is also precise - That it did not come to teach us [about] a coin.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:1:3.hebrew: כיצד החליף דמי שור בפרה - מכר לו שור במנה ומשכו, ונתחייב לו זה המנה. אמר לו המוכר: "יש לך פרה ליתן בדמים?" א"ל: "הן." שמאה לו במנה או בפרס. אמר לו מוכר השור: "הרי מעות שאתה חייב לי נתונים לך בדמיה." מעות הללו קונים בלא משיכת פרה, כחליפין דכלים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:1:3.english: How so? [If] one exchanged the value of an ox for a cow - [A person] sold him an ox for a maneh and [the buyer] pulled it, and this [buyer] became indebted to him [for] the maneh. The seller said to him: "Do you have a cow to give for the money?" He said to him: "Yes." He appraised it for him at a maneh or at a peras [half a maneh]. The seller of the ox said to him: "Behold, the money that you owe me is given to you for its purchase price." This money effects acquisition without the pulling of the cow, like the exchange of vessels.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:1:4.hebrew: מאי כיצד - ה"ל למיתני: כיצד החליף מעות בפרה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:1:4.english: What is [the meaning of] "How so" - [The Mishnah] should have taught: "How so? [If] one exchanged coins for a cow."

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:1:5.hebrew: מאי כיצד - ה"ל למיתני: כיצד החליף מעות בפרה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:1:5.english: What is “How so?” - [The Mishnah] should have taught: How so? [If] one exchanged coins for a cow.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:2:1.hebrew: מאי כיצד - ה"ל למיתני: כיצד? החליף מעות בפרה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:2:1.english: What is [the meaning of] "How so?" - It should have taught: "How so? [If] one exchanged coins for a cow."

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:2:2.hebrew: ה"ק כו' - תרתי אתא לאשמועינן: נקט ברישא מטבע, והדר אשמועינן שאר מטלטלין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:2:2.english: This is what [the mishna] is saying, etc. - [The mishna] came to teach us two [things]: it mentioned a coin in the first clause, and then it taught us [about] other movable items.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:2:3.hebrew: ופירי נמי כו' - כל מידי דלא הוי כלי, פירי קרי ליה לענין חליפין. ומשום דפירי שכיחי, נקט פירי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:2:3.english: And produce also, etc. - Anything that is not a utensil, [the Gemara] calls "produce" with regard to exchange; and because produce is common, it used [the term] "produce."

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:2:4.hebrew: עבדי חליפין - עושין תורת חליפין, ולא אמרינן נעל דוקא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:2:4.english: Effect exchange - They effect the law of exchange, and we do not say [that it must be] specifically a shoe.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:2:5.hebrew: בשר שור - וכ"ש שור חי, דעדיף טפי, דדמי לכלי שמשתמשין בו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:2:5.english: Meat of an ox - And all the more so a live ox, which is even better, as it is similar to a utensil that is used.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:3:1.hebrew: הניחא לרב ששת - איכא לתרוצי למתניתין, בין למאי דס"ד מעיקרא, בין למאי דתריצנא כל הנישום:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:3:1.english: This works out well according to Rav Sheshet - It is possible to explain the Mishnah both according to what initially entered [our] minds and according to how we resolved [it as] 'whatever is appraised.'

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:3:2.hebrew: אלא לר"נ - מאי כיצד למאי דס"ד מעיקרא? ואף למאי דאוקימנא נמי ליתא. פלוגתא דרב ששת ור"נ בפרק הזהב (ב"מ דף מז.):
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:3:2.english: But according to Rav Naḥman - What is [the meaning of] "How so?" according to what entered [our] minds initially? And even according to how we established [it], it is also not [tenable]. The dispute between Rav Sheshet and Rav Naḥman is in the chapter [entitled] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 47a).

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:3:3.english: What is the reason - [That it is] different from other money?

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:4:1.hebrew: ה"ק יש דמים שהן כחליפין - כולה מתני' חדא מילתא קאמר, ובמטבע עסקינן. וה"ק: כל הנעשה דמים באחר — דהיינו מטבע — פעמים שדמים קונים כמו חליפין דנעל, ואף כשנתנוהו בתורת דמים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:4:1.english: This is what it is saying: There is money that is like an exchange - The entire Mishnah is stating a single matter, and we are dealing with a coin. And this is what it is saying: "Whatever is used as payment for another" — that is, a coin — sometimes money effects acquisition like the exchange of a shoe, and even when they gave it in the capacity of payment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:4:2.hebrew: כיצד החליף דמי שור בפרה - מכר לו שור במנה, ומשכו, ונתחייב לו זה המנה. אמר לו המוכר: "יש לך פרה ליתן בדמים?" א"ל: "הן." שמאה לו במנה או בפרס. אמר לו מוכר השור: "הרי מעות שאתה חייב לי נתונים לך בדמיה." מעות הללו קונים בלא משיכת פרה, כחליפין דכלים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:4:2.english: How so? [If] one exchanged the monetary value of an ox for a cow - One sold [another] an ox for a mina, and [the buyer] pulled it, and this [buyer] became obligated to him [for] this mina. The seller said to him: “Do you have a cow to give in payment?” He said to him: “Yes.” He appraised it for him at a mina or at a paras. The seller of the ox said to him: “Behold, the money that you owe me is given to you as its price.” This money acquires [the cow] without pulling the cow, like the exchange of vessels.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:5:1.english: What is the reason - [That this case] is different from other [transactions with] money?

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:5:2.hebrew: סבר לה - תנא דמתני' כר' יוחנן דאמר כו', ומשיכה מדרבנן איתא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:5:2.english: He holds - The Tanna of our Mishnah [holds] in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said etc., and [the requirement of] pulling is Rabbinic.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:5:3.hebrew: שמא יאמר לו - המקבל מעות: "נשרפו חיטיך". אי מתרמי ליה דליקה, לא טרח לאצולינהו; סבר: "לא בשריפתן אפסיד, ולא בהצלתן אשתכר". להכי אוקמינהו ברשותיה, להיות הפסד השריפה עליו, והשכר לחזור אם נתייקרו — דלימסר נפשיה לאצולינהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:5:3.english: Lest he say to him - The recipient of the money [might say]: "Your wheat was burned." If a fire happens to occur, he will not bother to rescue it, [reasoning:] "I will not lose by its burning, nor will I gain by its rescue." For this reason, [the Sages] established it in his possession, so that the loss from the fire is upon him, and the benefit of retracting if it increases in price [is his] — so that he will exert himself to rescue it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:6:1.english: With regard to a common occurrence - Ordinary giving of money in a purchase.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:6:2.english: An uncommon occurrence - That [the seller] should owe him the money prior to that:

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:7:1.hebrew: משיכה מפורשת - ויליף לה מ"או קנה מיד עמיתך", ול"ש לא שכיחא מדשכיחא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:7:1.english: Pulling is explicitly stated - And he derives it from [the verse], “or buy from the hand of your fellow,” and there is no difference between an uncommon [occurrence] and a common [occurrence].

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:7:2.hebrew: הניחא אי סבר לה כרב ששת - דשאר מטלטלין שאינן כלי נעשה חליפין, מוקי למתניתין כרב ששת: "כל הנישום" כדאוקימנא, דהא אתא לאשמועינן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:7:2.english: This works out well if he holds in accordance with Rav Sheshet - That other movable property that is not a vessel can effect exchange; [and so] he can establish the Mishnah according to Rav Sheshet: [interpreting] “all that is appraised” as we established, for that is what [the Mishnah] comes to teach us.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:8:1.hebrew: אלא אי סבר לה כרב נחמן - דאמר נעל דוקא, דהוא כלי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:8:1.english: Rather, if he holds in accordance with Rav Naḥman - Who says [that the verse specifies] a “shoe” specifically, which is a utensil.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:8:2.hebrew: ומטבע לא קני - לר"ל מדאורייתא, דנימא "יש דמים שהם כחליפין" לאוקמי אדאורייתא במלתא דלא שכיח כדאוקמה ר"נ — היכי מתרץ לה למתניתין, בין לדסליק אדעתין מעיקרא, בין למאי דאוקימנא? יש משנין סוגיא של שמועה זו בשיטה אחרת, ואמרי: פלוגתא דר"נ ורב ששת בפירי דוקא, ולא בשאר מטלטלין, ומוליכין שיטת הסוגיא בתר מאי דסליק אדעתא מעיקרא; דלמאי דאוקימנא השתא מיתוקמא כר"נ שפיר, דמודה הוא בשאר מטלטלין. ולאו מילתא היא, דטעמא דר"נ מפורש בהזהב (דף מז.): דאמר קרא "נעל" — נעל, אין; מידי אחרינא, לא. וטעמא דרב ששת: "מלקיים כל דבר" — בכל דבר. ומטבע, היינו טעמא דלא עביד חליפין: משום דדעתיה אצורתא, וצורתא עבידא דבטלה, שהמלכות פוסלתה ואינה כלום:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:8:2.english: And a coin does not effect acquisition - [That is, it does not effect acquisition] according to Reish Lakish by Torah law, such that we could say "there is money that is like exchange" in order to establish [the Mishnah] according to Torah law in an uncommon case, as Rav Naḥman established it. [Therefore,] how can he explain the Mishnah, whether according to what entered our minds initially or according to what we established [it now]? Some alter the sugya of this report according to another approach, and say: The dispute between Rav Naḥman and Rav Sheshet is specifically regarding produce, and not regarding other movable property; and they direct the approach of the sugya following what entered the mind initially, for according to how we established it now, it would be established well in accordance with Rav Naḥman, as he concedes regarding other movable property. But this is incorrect, for the reasoning of Rav Naḥman is explicit in [the chapter entitled] HaZahav (47a): Scripture states, "a shoe" — a shoe, yes; anything else, no. And the reasoning of Rav Sheshet [is derived from], "to confirm all matters" — with any matter. And as for a coin, that is the reason it does not effect exchange: because one's mind is on the image, and the image is prone to become void, as the government may disqualify it and it becomes nothing.

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:9:1.hebrew: רשות הגבוה בכסף - בגמ' מפרש דמעות הקדש קונות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:9:1.english: The domain of the Most High [effects acquisition] with money - In the Gemara, it explains that consecrated money effects acquisition:

Rashi on Kiddushin 28b:9:3.english: One’s declaration to the Most High, etc. - It is explained in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 28b:5:1.hebrew: שמא יאמר לו נשרפו חיטיך בעלייה - ואם תאמר: אמאי עקרו קניית מעות שהם מדאורייתא לגמרי, ותקנו שתהא משיכה קונה ולא מעות? הוה להו לתקוני שיקנו המעות עם המשיכה, דהשתא לא מיעקרא קנייה דאורייתא לגמרי, וליכא נמי למיחש שמא יאמר המוכר "נשרפו חיטיך", כיון דמצי למיהדר ביה כל כמה דלא משך! וי"ל: דשמא לפעמים היה הלוקח מושך החיטין, ואי לא קנה במשיכה לחודה, יאמר למוכר "נשרפו חיטיך בעלייה". וא"ת: השתא נמי, כיון דמעות אינן קונות, לפעמים יתן הלוקח מעות למוכר קודם שימשוך החיטין, ויאמר המוכר "נשרפו מעותיך בעלייה"? וי"ל: דלהא ליכא למיחש, דלכל הפחות יהא המוכר כשומר חנם, דמעות וכספים אין להם שמירה אלא בקרקע, והתם לא שייך למימר "נשרפו מעותיך":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 28b:5:1.english: "Lest he say to him: Your wheat was burned in the loft" - And if you say: Why did they completely uproot the acquisition [effected by] money, which is by Torah law, and enact that pulling acquires and not money? They should have enacted that money acquires along with pulling, for then the Torah acquisition would not be completely uprooted, and there would also be no concern lest the seller say "Your wheat was burned," since he can retract as long as [the buyer] has not pulled [the wheat]! And one can say: That perhaps sometimes the buyer would pull the wheat, and if he did not acquire through pulling alone, he would say to the seller: "Your wheat was burned in the loft." And if you say: Now too, since money does not acquire, sometimes the buyer will give money to the seller before he pulls the wheat, and the seller will say: "Your money was burned in the loft"? And one can say: That regarding this there is no concern, for at the very least the seller would be like an unpaid bailee, and money and coins have no safeguard except in the ground, and there it is not applicable to say "Your money was burned."
